title: Combined picture: agentproto + agent2agent
summary: Both lists are now shown together rather than one standing in for the other. Topics from every list share one graph, activity is summed with a per-list split, and thread axes are reported per list because pooling them is exactly how a 15-origin finding from a three-week-old list became a claim about the method.

focus.title: 79% of agentproto also posts on agent2agent
focus.ask: 22 of 28. Does that change what agentproto is to you — a new venue for the same people rather than a new audience?
focus.watch: The per-list chips and the cross-list count sit above the tiles.

focus.title: Volume is now summed across both lists
focus.ask: The window still defaults to 7 days. With one list 483 days old and the other 22, is a shared window useful, or do you want the range per list?
focus.watch: Compare the combined line against the per-list chips — agent2agent dominates.

focus.title: One graph, topics from both lists
focus.ask: agentproto contributes zero topics because the blob cap refuses to split its 23 threads. Should its threads still appear in the graph as unassigned, or is a list with no topics better left out entirely?
focus.watch: Expand a topic — the layout animates rather than jumping. Clusters are seeded apart before the force pass.

focus.title: Thread axes, per list, with the withdrawn verdict stated
focus.ask: The open/narrow/closed label inverted and was removed. Is stating the removal on the page right, or does an admission of a withdrawn measure belong only in the docs?
focus.watch: Reach differs sharply between the lists. Uptake medians are close.

focus.title: Nothing beats counting replies
focus.ask: On agent2agent's 159 origins the baseline wins: +0.462 against novelty's +0.419 and standing's +0.403. Does that change what you want built next, or is the corpus still too small to act on?
focus.watch: The three cards below the graph.
